sentences.text:
2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
Sharbhaiah.M vs Kumar on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159004307/
1

That on on 21.10.2021 at about 03.35 PM., near Muthu garage, in Horamavu main road, Bangalore wherein the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-AD- 7574 drove it, in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle, which was left by him for the repair work in Muthu garage, and caused the accident.
In the accident the petitioner vehicle was damaged.
Petitioner got repaired his damage vehicle and spent Rs.25,000/-.
He alleged that he is an electrician and he has spent Rs.81,000/- for his movements in 270 days as traveling expenses and he has incurred Rs.5,000/- for miscellaneous expenses.

He alleged that respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending lorry he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2 and they are jointly liable to pay the vehicle damage cost and prays this court to allowing the petition.

3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle has not appeared before the tribunal to contest the petition, he placed exparte.
4. Respondent No.2 being the insurer has appeared through his counsel, filed Vakalath and written statement by denying the entire petition averments in toto.
He specifically contended that the petitioner has planted the vehicle with an intention to claim the vehicle damages and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined another witness as PW-2 produced and marked 9 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 9 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent No.2 has not chosen to lead his evidence after obtaining sufficient opportunity from this Tribunal accordingly respondent evidence is taken as nil 6.
I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that his two wheeler Bajaj V15 bearing No.KA-04-JD- 6122 was damaged on 21.10.2021 at about 3.35 PM., on Kalkere to Horamavu main road, near Muthu Motor works garage, Bangalore, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-02-AD-7574?
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

Sharbhaiah.M vs Kumar on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159004307/
2 8.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, final report, sketch,
mahazar, IMV report, which are at Ex.P.1 to 6.
The said documents are not disputed nor denied by the respondent no.2 10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Kumar S/o Late Venkatesh.
The involvement of the two wheeler is not disputed nor denied by the respondent.
It is also true that driver of the offending vehicle has admitted his guilt and paid the fine amount in Cr.No.130/2021 before the MMTC court-1.
Ex.P6 is the IMV report, it recitals reveals that vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-04-JD-6122 is damaged and three damages are reported therein.
In the cross examination of PW-1, nothing is elicited to disprove his allegation.
PW-2 is informant in the alleged crime.
According to him he is the mechanic who repaired the damaged vehicle of the petition.
He has tendered the estimation and bill for the spare parts and labour charges.
In his cross examination he clearly admitted that he has not tendered the invoice and cash paid receipts for having purchased the spare parts alleged to has used for repairing the petitioner vehicle.

The vehicle damages reported in IMV report and the spare parts details as stated by PW-2, the details of estimation which is at Ex.P9 are not corroborating with each other and they are inconsistent to each other.
Accordingly the testimony of PW-2 is not worthy and version of the PW-1 cannot be accepted in full.

Considering the facts and attending circumstance and IMV report, the cost of the vehicle damages that is head light mask, crash guard, mirrors, indicators, hand grip and Gear lever dislocation, as stated in IMV report can be assessed as Rs.9,000/- including the spare parts and labour charges.
11. Petitioner has not established the fact that he is an electrician and he has incurred traveling and miscellaneous expenses as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly the said expenses cannot be accepted without tantamount documents and petitioner is not entitled for the same.
12. Liability :
The respondent no.2 is the insurer of offending vehicle and the validity of the policy of the said vehicle is not in dispute.

Inasmuch respondent no.2 is liable to pay the cost of vehicle damages, therefore respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the cost of vehicle damages amount as discussed above within 30 days of judgment.

Accordingly I answer Issue no.1 in the affirmative,
Issue no.2 in Partly affirmative.

; For the foregoing reason and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner under Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the cost of the vehicle damages amount of Rs.9,000/-.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the cost of vehicle damages amount before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the cost of damages amount, petitioner is permitted to withdraw the entire cost of damages amount by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt.
17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
